newsitem.title: FRANCE: Sogaris freight handling extension to open in May.
newsitem.headline: Sogaris freight handling extension to open in May.

text.p: French freight-handling installations operator, Sogaris, said the extension of its existing facilities at Paris-Charles de Gaulle (CDG) airport will enter service at start of May this year.
"The extension will provide an additional 10,000 sq metres of warehousing and 2,200 sq. metres of office space," Sogaris' marketing and sales director, Jacques Salgues, told Reuters.
Salgues added: "There is a real demand for warehousing and office facilities at CDG and we are confident that the additional space offered by the extension will be let fairly quickly."

Around 20 airfreight forwarders and agents occupy Sogaris' existing Centre Logistique de Fret Aerien in CDG's freight zone. This comprises 18,000 sq. metres of warehousing and 4,000 sq.metres of offices.
With airside access, the Sogaris centre is equipped with loading platforms for truck-borne freight and also houses a customs office.
The extension, costing 60 million francs, is being financed by a joint-venture company, 60 percent-owned by Sogaris and 40 percent by the Paris airports authority.
Sogaris was also considering further development of its CDG facilities, Salgues said.
Sogaris is 80 percent-owned by public authorities in the Paris area with the remaining 20 percent owned by private investors.
